# Strings {.unnumbered}

A string is a `char` array ending in `'\0'` — the **null terminator**. There is no string type.

## Declaring

```c
char s[] = "level";      /* 6 chars: l e v e l \0 — writable copy */
char big[20] = "hello";  /* 20 chars, room to grow                */
char *p = "level";       /* points at a literal — DO NOT modify   */
```

| index | 0 | 1 | 2 | 3 | 4 | 5 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `char s[] = "level"` | `l` | `e` | `v` | `e` | `l` | `\0` |

## sizeof vs strlen

```
char s[] = "level";
sizeof s  = 6      all the boxes, including the '\0'
strlen(s) = 5      characters before the '\0'
```

| | answered | survives being passed to a function |
|---|---|---|
| `sizeof` | at compile time | **no** — gives the pointer size |
| `strlen` | at run time, by walking | yes |

## string.h

| | |
|---|---|
| `strlen(s)` | characters before the `'\0'` |
| `strcpy(dst, src)` | copy, terminator included |
| `strcat(dst, src)` | append |
| `strcmp(a, b)` | **0 means equal**; sign otherwise |

```c
char big[20] = "hello";       /* room to grow — this matters */
strcat(big, " there");        /* big is now "hello there"    */

strcmp("abc", "abc")          /*  0        */
strcmp("Zebra", "apple")      /*  negative  ('Z' is 90, 'a' is 97) */
```

::: {.callout-important}
The first argument to `strcpy` and `strcat` must be a **writable array with room**. Never a string literal: `strcat("hello", " there")` compiles without a warning and then crashes.
:::

::: {.callout-warning}
`strcmp` is **not alphabetical** — it compares character codes, and every capital sorts before every lowercase.

`strcpy` and `strcat` do **not** check that the destination is big enough.
:::

## Walking

```c
int n = 0;
while (s[n] != '\0') n++;        /* length by hand */

for (int i = 0; s[i] != '\0'; i++)
    …s[i]…
```

## Reading

```c
char w[50];
scanf("%49s", w);     /* no &; limit is one less than the size */
```

`%s` stops at the first **whitespace** — space, tab or newline. One word, not a line.

## Characters

| Test | |
|---|---|
| is a letter | `(c>='a'&&c<='z') \|\| (c>='A'&&c<='Z')` |
| is a digit | `c >= '0' && c <= '9'` |
| digit to number | `c - '0'` |

**Changing case needs a guard.** The formulas only work on a letter already in the other case, and give nonsense otherwise:

```c
char toUpper(char c) {
    if (c >= 'a' && c <= 'z') return c - 'a' + 'A';
    return c;                      /* leave everything else alone */
}
char toLower(char c) {
    if (c >= 'A' && c <= 'Z') return c - 'A' + 'a';
    return c;
}
```

Applied without the guard: `'5' - 'a' + 'A'` is 21, and `'a' - 'A' + 'a'` overflows a signed `char` to −127.

`'a' - 'A'` is 32, but write `- 'a' + 'A'`: it says what it means.

::: {.callout-note}
`<ctype.h>` provides `isalpha`, `isdigit`, `isspace`, `toupper`, `tolower`, already guarded. Writing them by hand once is the exercise; using the library afterwards is sensible.
:::

## Traps

| | |
|---|---|
| forgetting the `'\0'` | every string function runs off the end |
| `sizeof` for the length after passing | gives the pointer size |
| `if (strcmp(a,b))` | true when they **differ** |
| modifying `char *p = "literal"` | **undefined behaviour** |
| `scanf("%s", s)` with no limit | writes past the array |
